html:
Óscar Romero was the archbishop of San Salvador from 1977 until he was shot dead while saying mass on 24 March 1980. In 2018 the Catholic Church declared him a saint.

He was chosen as a safe conservative, but the murder of his friend, the Jesuit priest Rutilio Grande, in 1977 changed him. In weekly sermons broadcast across El Salvador, he named the killings and disappearances carried out by the army and death squads. He drew on liberation theology and its call to stand with the poor.

The day before his death he begged soldiers to stop killing their own people. A UN truth commission later found that a death squad organised by Roberto D'Aubuisson, founder of the right-wing ARENA party, killed him. Gunfire at his funeral killed dozens. His murder marked the start of the civil war, and he is honoured across the Catholic world.
